recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-26859 unless a future work group decision reopens the set of Procedure.subject targets or deliberately adds another target such as RegulatedAuthorization.
issue_request: FHIR-26859 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It requested keeping Procedure.subject at 1..1 while expanding the allowed reference targets beyond Patient and Group to include Device, Practitioner, Organization, and Location, and updating the Procedure definition, subject short/definition, and scope text for non-patient procedures such as inspections and licensing.
initial_application: The issue was applied by b91c941c0d72e2291ac6ec3729c92af941f7216b, which changed the then-authoritative Procedure spreadsheet from Reference(Patient|Group) to Reference(Patient|Group|Device|Practitioner|Organization|Location), added the J#26859 notes, and updated the Procedure introduction narrative. The later source rework in 33b409a4b6 preserved the same target list and wording in structuredefinition-Procedure.xml and procedure-introduction.xml.
additional_context: The active source/fhir.ini resource entry includes procedure=Procedure, so the Procedure resource folder is in current build scope. The current Procedure.subject definition includes later Procedure.focus clarification text, but that later wording does not reverse or narrow the FHIR-26859 target expansion. The linked Zulip discussion and Confluence references align with the Jira rationale that Procedure needed to support non-patient subjects; no conflicting community evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made because Procedure.subject remains 1..1 and references Patient, Group, Device, Practitioner, Organization, and Location; the resource definition and scope narrative describe procedures on or for patients, practitioners, devices, organizations, and locations; and the subject short/definition reflects individuals or entities.
